title: EXP-132 — FX_ Web User Control Bridge via Form Variable Readback
objective: Determine whether an existing FX_ Web User Control can invoke the existing FX_Echo C# Form Script method and then obtain the expected string through WSForm.getVarValue. Preserve FX_BridgeTest and FX_BridgeControl; create exactly one FX_vEcho variable of the documented appropriate scope and persistence type; extend FX_Echo to assign FX_ECHO: plus its argument to that variable while retaining its existing string return; and update FX_Bridge/index.html to display the raw invocation callback value separately in FX_BridgeStatus before requesting FX_vEcho through getVarValue. After one ordinary Designer Form Save and one close/reopen readback, perform exactly one runtime activation. Success requires visible FX_BridgeOutput text FX_ECHO:bridge-probe and a recorded FX_BridgeStatus value. A different result is recorded as an unsuccessful observation without retry or alternate API calls.

in_scope: Read AGENTS.md, EXP-131's final evidence manifest and existing bridge definitions before performing any mutation.

Read the saved evidence copies evidence/EXP-128/MockInventoryDashboard-form-script.cs.txt, evidence/EXP-128/assets/MockInventory_index.html.txt, and evidence/EXP-130/T2-designer-metadata-gaps.txt to establish the exact documented variable-write and getVarValue usage. These are read-only source references, not permission to open Mock objects.

Perform the same owner-account and isolation preflight as EXP-131 T1: record the Web Client account header; confirm FX_CustomerPortal is present; confirm MockLoginPortal and FX_InventoryPrototype01 are absent from the relevant visible Form inventory; and confirm FX_BridgeTest is present as the current operator's User-scoped version. Verify Designer cleanliness, console baselines, and no open dialogs.
Inspect the existing FX_BridgeTest variable definitions and prove that FX_vEcho does not already exist before creating it. Record all existing UserCtrl variables without modifying them.

Create exactly one variable FX_vEcho through the supported Designer Variables interface. Prefer Global=True and Persistent=True, matching the documented vInventoryJson metadata. If specialist guidance establishes that a Form-level variable is required for this getVarValue use case, require explicit coordinator disposition before selecting that alternative. Record the actual category, Global and Persistent settings, and justification.

Modify only the existing FX_Echo method inside FX_BridgeTest. Preserve the Mongoose.FormScripts scaffold, method signature and existing return value. Add the supported equivalent of ThisForm.Variables("FX_vEcho").Value = "FX_ECHO:" + s; before the existing return statement. Verify the exact source readback and inspect Compile Result if the supported editor exposes it.

Modify only FX_Bridge/index.html, preserving its existing UserControl.js dependency, FX_BridgeButton, FX_BridgeOutput and invocation signature. Add one FX_BridgeStatus element. Have the existing invoke callback write its received value to FX_BridgeStatus, then request FX_vEcho with exactly one WSForm.getVarValue call and write the received variable value to FX_BridgeOutput. Follow the documented Mock callback pattern rather than inventing alternate APIs.
Retain the existing FX_BridgeControl component and verify that its Use Web Control setting and Control URL FX_Bridge/index.html are unchanged.

Commit through the supported variable, Script Editor and Web Asset editor controls. Perform exactly one ordinary Designer Form Save after the planned definition changes, followed by exactly one ordinary Designer Form close and reopen and read-only verification of the retained variable, script, HTML and UserControl reference.

Perform exactly one runtime FX_BridgeTest Form open and one FX_BridgeButton activation. Capture the visible pre-click empty output, the post-click FX_BridgeStatus callback value, and the post-click FX_BridgeOutput variable value. Close the experiment-opened runtime Form without saving if no stop condition is triggered.

Record every created or modified artifact, browser action/read count, console comparison, Save count, lifecycle operation, runtime activation and evidence path under evidence/EXP-132/. Keep findings classified as observed or unresolved, without claiming replay verification.
out_of_scope: Changes to any non-FX_ artifact, including MockLoginPortal, MockInventory, MockInventoryDashboard, MockLoginIDO, FX_InventoryPrototype01 and any $app asset.
Reading, editing or replacing the live shared $app/scripts/UserControl.js.
Changes to FX_BridgeControl's name, type, reference, placement or existing settings.
Deletion or cleanup of stale UserCtrl_userControl1_USER, UserCtrlAsm_userControl1_USER, UserCtrlUrl_userControl1_USER or any other automatically generated variable.
Creating additional variables, methods, components, Forms, IDOs, SQL tables, property classes, event handlers, global scripts or other global objects beyond FX_vEcho.
Replaying EXP-131's previous runtime test without the new variable-readback implementation.
Debugging the internal meaning of WSForm.invoke callback result 0 or claiming it is a status code without supporting evidence.
Cross-session database durability, cache internals, FormSync, deployment, metadata regeneration or global-object unloading.
Authentication or account changes, credentials, unrelated application data, and other Users' Form versions.

prohibited_actions: Creating, modifying or deleting any non-FX_ artifact
Starting any other experiment or replay
Modifying production data or disabling security
Reading or printing credential values
Do not start this proposal before operator approval.
Do not mutate anything before completing the account, scope, identity, cleanliness and target-baseline gates.
Do not sign in, deliberately reauthenticate, switch accounts or change editing scope during the experiment. Stop if the required authenticated session is unavailable.
Do not open, edit, save or delete a Mock object, FX_InventoryPrototype01 or a $app asset. Read only the existing repository evidence copies.

Do not execute browser JavaScript, page.evaluate, synthetic DOM scripts or internal application APIs. Set worker_tool_policy deny_browser_javascript true. JavaScript authored inside the approved FX_Bridge/index.html asset is allowed.
Do not inspect or alter the live UserControl.js file.
Do not create FX_vEcho if the name already exists or its intended Global/Persistent settings cannot be confirmed. Do not silently substitute a temporary or Form-level variable.
Do not replace the FX_Echo method signature, delete its existing return statement, create a second FX_Echo method or change unrelated script scaffolding.
Do not add alternate WSForm.invoke or WSForm.getVarValue signatures, extra callbacks, polling, retries or fallback mechanisms.
Do not remove, recreate, rename or otherwise modify FX_BridgeControl or generated UserCtrl variables.
Do not invoke Regenerate Form, Unload All Global Form Objects, metadata-cache clearing, FormSync, IDO maintenance, database operations or deployment.
Never activate Designer's top-toolbar Delete Form Definition control.
Do not perform more than one ordinary Designer Form Save or more than one prescribed Designer Form close/reopen without additional operator authorization.
Do not activate FX_BridgeButton more than once, even if the displayed result is empty, 0, delayed or unexpected.
If a compile error, unexpected dialog, scope mismatch, console increase, guard/hook failure, unsupported UI or ambiguous mutation appears, stop without a workaround or additional mutation.

Limit browser recovery to one fresh snapshot and one corrected inspection for the experiment. After exhausting either allowance or encountering a guard/hook failure, stop rather than broadening recovery.
Do not delete or clean up any existing FX_ artifact after a failed test.
prohibited_patterns: \b(?:invoke|execute|activate|click)\b[^\n]{0,60}\b(?:Unload All Global Form Objects|FormSync|Delete Form Definition|Regenerate Form)\b

acceptance_checks.description: Preflight identity and isolation gate: evidence/EXP-132/ contains a screenshot or captured accessibility readback identifying the Web Client account as the operator-confirmed account, the Designer User scope and FX_BridgeTest User version, FX_CustomerPortal present, MockLoginPortal and FX_InventoryPrototype01 absent in the tested visible inventory, and the initial clean Form and console baselines. If any required gate fails, no mutation occurs.

Baseline and source-pattern gate: the worker captures the original FX_BridgeTest C# method, FX_Bridge/index.html contents, FX_BridgeControl reference, visible existing variables and absence of FX_vEcho. The worker identifies the precise saved Mock evidence lines supporting the variable assignment, invoke followed by getVarValue, and variable metadata. Any uncertainty in the required variable type is resolved by documented specialist guidance and coordinator approval before mutation.

Exactly one FX_vEcho variable is created through the supported Designer UI. Evidence visibly identifies its name, variable category and Global/Persistent settings, normally Global=True and Persistent=True. No other named variable is created, renamed or deleted.

FX_BridgeTest's C# Script Editor readback shows exactly one FX_Echo(string s) method that writes FX_ECHO: plus s to FX_vEcho and retains return "FX_ECHO:" + s. Existing class and namespace scaffolding are preserved. A supported Compile Result view is captured if available; an empty result is not described as affirmative proof of successful compilation.

FX_Bridge/index.html readback shows one FX_BridgeButton, one FX_BridgeOutput and one newly added FX_BridgeStatus, with the original script dependency preserved. The single invoke callback records its received result in FX_BridgeStatus and issues one getVarValue request for FX_vEcho, whose callback writes to FX_BridgeOutput. The unchanged FX_BridgeControl reference to FX_Bridge/index.html is independently shown. Evidence is captured before committing the asset changes.

Exactly one ordinary Designer Form Save returns the Designer to a clean state. After one ordinary Form close and reopen, evidence confirms FX_BridgeTest User identity, FX_vEcho metadata, the revised FX_Echo method, the revised asset contents, the existing FX_BridgeControl reference, and Save disabled. This is same-session UI-level recovery evidence only.

The Web Client opens exactly one runtime FX_BridgeTest instance. A pre-activation screenshot shows the bridge button and empty result fields. After exactly one click, a decisive screenshot visibly identifies the runtime Form, FX_BridgeStatus value and FX_BridgeOutput value. Success requires FX_BridgeOutput to display the exact literal FX_ECHO:bridge-probe and FX_BridgeStatus to display the observed invoke callback value. Otherwise AC-7 is failed, without retry or alternate invocation.

The experiment-opened runtime Form is closed once without saving when safe to do so. The Web Client has no remaining experiment-created runtime tab, and the Designer remains on FX_BridgeTest with Save disabled and no unexpected dialog. Before/after console counters and the closure state are captured. If a stop rule prevents cleanup, the actual remaining state is reported without claiming this check passed.

A final evidence manifest under evidence/EXP-132/ reconciles every modified FX_ object, exactly one planned variable creation, one Designer Save, one Form close/reopen, one runtime activation, browser action/read totals, recovery usage and repository confinement. Operator Git review verifies only the approved EXP-132 record and evidence directory are attributable tracked changes. Every unresolved compilation, callback, persistence or runtime question is explicitly retained.

initial_instruction: PROPOSAL ONLY UNTIL OPERATOR APPROVAL. Once approved, execute EXP-132 in separate, small, coordinator-authorized tasks. Set worker_tool_policy deny_browser_javascript true. Start with a read-only T1 that reviews AGENTS.md, EXP-131, and the cited EXP-128/EXP-130 evidence copies; captures the account and Form identity/isolation gates; confirms the Designer is clean; and records the initial script, asset, reference and variable baselines. Do not mutate in T1. Before variable creation, establish the supported variable type: prefer the documented Global Persistent kind, and stop for specialist/coordinator disposition if getVarValue requires a different supported definition. Then create only FX_vEcho and verify its definition; modify only the existing FX_Echo method and inspect its readback and available Compile Result; modify only FX_Bridge/index.html to separate invoke callback status from the FX_vEcho getVarValue result; perform one ordinary Form Save after all planned edits; perform one ordinary close/reopen and verify retention; then perform one runtime open, one button activation and one ordinary close if safe. Record visible FX_BridgeStatus and FX_BridgeOutput separately, without assuming the callback value means success or failure. At every boundary capture decisive screenshots or readbacks identifying target, scope and outcome under evidence/EXP-132/. All mutations are FX_-only; no Mock or $app object access, browser JavaScript execution, cleanup, alternate API attempts, extra Saves, regeneration, cache unload or FormSync. Use at most one fresh recovery snapshot and one corrected inspection across the experiment; stop on an unresolved failed action or guard/hook error. The worker must stop at each authorized task boundary and report to the coordinator. The experiment is not considered successful unless the exact runtime output FX_ECHO:bridge-probe is visibly observed after the single authorized click.
notes: Proposed by the coordinator after run R-20261025-203228-l0nq. Rationale: EXP-131 established that FX_BridgeTest, its C# Form Script, Web User Control Asset and UserControl reference survive the prescribed Save and close/reopen sequence, and that the bridge button renders at runtime. However, the single runtime activation displayed 0 rather than FX_ECHO:bridge-probe. The operator identified a distinct documented pattern in the Mock Inventory application: a Form Script method writes data to ThisForm.Variables, and the Web User Control calls WSForm.invoke followed by WSForm.getVarValue to obtain that data. EXP-132 will test this explicitly different approach as a new experiment, not replay or repair EXP-131. The meaning of the previous callback value 0 remains an unverified hypothesis.
